summary.text: Resonance happens when an outside force or vibration repeats at a frequency that matches a natural resonant frequency of a system.
The system then absorbs energy from the force and vibrates with a much larger amplitude, even when each push is small.
This is useful in musical instruments and radio receivers, but it can also cause excessive vibration or even structural failure.

facts.label: Playground swing
facts.value: Pushes timed to its natural rhythm make it go higher

facts.label: Word origin
facts.value: From Latin for echo, first used in acoustics

facts.label: Small damping
facts.value: Resonant frequency is close to the natural frequency

facts.label: Where it occurs
facts.value: Mechanical, acoustic, electromagnetic, orbital and nuclear systems

items.prompt: You push a child on a swing every time it returns to you. Why does the swing climb higher with each push?

options.label: Each push adds an equal fixed height
Timed pushes match its natural rhythm and add up
A faster push cancels the swing's damping
The swing gets lighter as it rises

items.explain: The energy the swing absorbs is largest when pushes match its natural oscillations.

items.prompt: Another parent pushes the swing at a much faster tempo than its natural one. What is the likely result?

options.label: The biggest swing of the day
The swing stops moving instantly
Only small swings
The swing turns into a driven pendulum

items.explain: Pushing faster or slower than the natural tempo produces smaller swings, because less energy is absorbed.

items.prompt: A footbridge starts shaking harder when many walkers step in a steady rhythm. Which idea explains why it might even fail?

options.label: Resonance can drive excessive vibration and structural failure
Heavier crowds make bridges lighter
Steady steps remove all damping
A matching rhythm lowers the bridge's frequency

items.explain: Resonance can lead to excessive vibrations or even structural failure when forcing matches the system's resonant frequency.

items.prompt: A radio picks out one station from many broadcasting at once. Which feature of resonant systems does that rely on?

options.label: Absorbing every frequency equally
Blocking all vibration entirely
Turning a single tone into many
Picking out one frequency from a mix

items.explain: Resonant systems can pick out specific frequencies from a complex vibration containing many frequencies, as in filters and radio receivers.

items.prompt: A guitar string is plucked and a nearby string of the same pitch starts to hum. What does this show?

options.label: A matching vibration can set a system moving
Strings always share their energy equally
Quiet sounds cannot cause vibration
Resonance needs two different pitches

items.explain: Resonance comes from an outside vibration at the system's resonant frequency, and the word originated in acoustics with sympathetic vibration.

items.prompt: A system has very low damping. How does its resonant frequency compare with its natural frequency?

options.label: Much higher than it
Roughly equal to it
Much lower than it
Unrelated to it

items.explain: When damping is small, the resonant frequency is approximately equal to the natural frequency of unforced vibration.
